description: Special instructions (SPINS) are a publication that adds procedures, restrictions and coordination instructions to the tasking of all missions. It contains permanent instructions, or changes to a base publication with a pinned reference.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

air_defense.description: This field gives the air defence procedures.

airspace_notes.description: This list contains the airspace notes.

base.description: This field identifies the base publication that this publication changes. The reference identifies one revision of the publication.

cas.description: This field gives the close air support (CAS) stacks, the laser code plan and the laser restrictions.

changes.description: This list contains the changes to the base publication, in order. A consumer makes the changes in the sequence of the list.

check_in.description: This list contains the procedures for each agency at the start and at the end of a task.

communications.description: This field gives the radio nets and the brevity words.

divert_and_abort.description: This field gives the abort conditions and the divert airfields.

electromagnetic.description: This field gives the emission control periods and the jamming coordination.

emergency.description: This field gives the emergency procedures.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record. The namespace `org.opord-builder.print` contains the data that `opord-builder` puts on each page.

identification.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) assignments and code words.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a special instructions (SPINS) publication.

meta.description: This field gives the identification, revision and issue data of this document.

night_operations.description: This field gives the night vision goggles (NVG) procedures, the lights-out areas and the lighting rules.

orders.description: This field gives the operation order (OPORD), the air tasking order (ATO) and the airspace control order (ACO) of the publication.

period.description: This field gives the time interval during which the instructions are in effect.

personnel_recovery.description: This field gives the combat search and rescue (CSAR) and personnel recovery procedures.

recovery_routing.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) lines, the routes back and the recovery airfields.

references.description: This list contains the coordination documents for the publication, such as the air tasking order (ATO) or the airspace control order (ACO).

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the publication, as free text.

reports.description: This list contains the report requirements for aircrews, such as the mission report (MISREP), the in-flight report and the battle damage assessment (BDA) report.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this publication.

restrictions.description: This field gives the protected sites and the weather minimums.

rules_of_engagement.description: This field gives the rules of engagement (ROE) summary.

schema_version.description: This field gives the version of the openAIX schema that this document agrees with.

scope.description: This field gives the type of the instructions: permanent instructions (`standing`) or instructions for one mission (`mission`), as one of the enumerated values.

tanker_procedures.description: This list contains the tanker procedures.

title: openAIX SPINS

AbortCriterion.description: An abort condition is one condition that stops a mission, and the procedure of the aircrew.

action.description: This field gives the procedure of the aircrew, as one of the enumerated values.

condition.description: This field gives the condition, as free text.

id.description: This field identifies this abort condition. Each abort condition in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this abort condition.

AbortCriterion.title: AbortCriterion

AirDefenseWarning.description: An air defence warning is one air defence warning for an area and a time interval.

level.description: This field gives the air defence warning, as one of the enumerated values.

measure.description: This field identifies the control measure that gives the area of the air defence warning.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the air defence warning is in effect.

AirDefenseWarning.title: AirDefenseWarning

AirspaceNote.description: An airspace note is one note about control measures for aircrews.

id.description: This field identifies this note. Each note in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this note.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that the note refers to.

note.description: This field gives the note, as free text.

AirspaceNote.title: AirspaceNote

BearingSector.description: A direction sector is the sector of directions clockwise from the value of `from` to the value of `to`.

from.description: This field gives the first bearing of the sector, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

to.description: This field gives the second bearing of the sector, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

BearingSector.title: BearingSector

BrevityTerm.description: A brevity word is one brevity word and its definition for this operation.

id.description: This field identifies this brevity word. Each brevity word in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this brevity word.

meaning.description: This field gives the definition of the brevity word, as free text.

term.description: This field gives the brevity word, as free text.

BrevityTerm.title: BrevityTerm

CasStack.description: A close air support (CAS) stack is one holding stack for CAS aircraft above a point or an orbit.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that assigns the levels of the stack.

id.description: This field identifies this stack. Each stack in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this stack.

levels.description: This list contains the levels of the stack, from the top, in order.

name.description: This field gives the name of this stack, for display.

orbit.description: This field identifies the orbit that is the holding pattern of the stack. The measure shall be an orbit.

point.description: This field identifies the point that is the centre of the stack. The point shall have the role `marshalling` or `control` or `initial`.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the stack, as free text.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the stack is in effect.

CasStack.title: CasStack

CheckInProcedure.description: An agency procedure is the procedure when aircrews start and stop the communication with one agency.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the first message of the aircrews.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that aircrews contact the agency on.

check_in_items.description: This list contains the items that aircrews give when they first contact the agency, in order, in order.

check_out.description: This field gives the instructions for the end of the communication, as free text.

contact_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the point at which aircrews first contact the agency. The point shall have the role `control`.

id.description: This field identifies this procedure. Each procedure in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this procedure.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure of the resource catalogue that gives the steps.

CheckInProcedure.title: CheckInProcedure

CodeWord.description: A code word is one code word and its definition for a time interval.

id.description: This field identifies this code word. Each code word in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this code word.

meaning.description: This field gives the definition of the code word, as free text.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the code word is in effect.

word.description: This field gives the code word, as free text.

CodeWord.title: CodeWord

CommitCriterion.description: A commit criterion is one condition at which fighters fly to intercept a track.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the tracks that cause the commit, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use this commit criterion. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

commit_range.description: This field gives the distance from the fighters to the track at the commit, as a length with its unit.

declarations.description: This list contains the declarations that a track has before a commit.

id.description: This field identifies this commit criterion. Each commit criterion in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this commit criterion.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area in which a track causes the commit.

orbit.description: This field identifies the orbit that the fighters fly before the commit. The measure shall be an orbit.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure of the resource catalogue that gives the steps of the commit.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about this commit criterion, as free text.

threats.description: This list identifies the threats of the resource catalogue that this commit criterion is for.

CommitCriterion.title: CommitCriterion

DamagedAircraftRoute.description: A route for an aircraft with damage is the route that an aircraft with damage or an emergency flies to an airfield.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the first call of the aircraft.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that receives the aircraft.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that the aircraft uses.

condition.description: This field gives the condition for the route, as one of the enumerated values.

id.description: This field identifies this route. Each route in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this route.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that the aircraft flies. Each measure shall have the type `MRR` or `SC` or `TC` or `AIRCOR` or `SAAFR` or `LLTR`.

routes.description: This list identifies the routes of the resource catalogue that the aircraft flies.

squawk.description: This field gives the Mode 3/A code that the aircraft sets, as four octal digits.

DamagedAircraftRoute.title: DamagedAircraftRoute

DivertAirfield.description: A divert airfield is one airfield for diversion, with its priority.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that is the divert airfield.

conditions.description: This field gives the conditions for a diversion to the airfield, as free text.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of this entry. The value 1 is the highest priority.

DivertAirfield.title: DivertAirfield

EmissionControlPeriod.description: An emission control period is one emission control level for a time interval.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that the level is applicable to. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

id.description: This field identifies this period. Each period in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this period.

level.description: This field gives the emission control level, as one of the enumerated values.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area of the level.

units.description: This list identifies the units of the task organization that the level is applicable to.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the level is in effect.

EmissionControlPeriod.title: EmissionControlPeriod

IdentificationCriterion.description: An identification matrix row is one row of the identification matrix: a declaration and the conditions that give it.

authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that makes the declaration.

criteria.description: This list contains the conditions of the declaration.

declaration.description: This field gives the declaration that the conditions give, as one of the enumerated values.

id.description: This field identifies this row. Each row in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this row.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area where this row is applicable.

minimum_criteria.description: This field gives the number of conditions that are necessary for the declaration.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about this row, as free text.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which this row is in effect.

IdentificationCriterion.title: IdentificationCriterion

IffAssignment.description: An identification, friend or foe (IFF) assignment is one IFF mode and code for a time interval.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the code. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

code.description: This field gives the code, as two or four octal digits. Modes 4 and 5 use key names, not codes, and do not have this field.

id.description: This field identifies this assignment. Each assignment in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this assignment.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the areas or lines where the code changes, such as `IFFON` and `IFFOFF` lines.

mode.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode, as one of the enumerated values.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the code is in effect.

IffAssignment.title: IffAssignment

JammingCoordination.description: A jamming coordination is one time interval of electromagnetic attack, with its emitters and the frequencies that it keeps clear.

area.description: This field identifies the area of the resource catalogue that the jamming aircraft operate in.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that do the jamming. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives approval for the jamming.

emitters.description: This list identifies the emitters of the resource catalogue that are the objects of the jamming.

id.description: This field identifies this entry. Each entry in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this entry.

protected_frequencies.description: This list contains the frequencies that the jamming does not have an effect on.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the jamming occurs.

JammingCoordination.title: JammingCoordination

JettisonArea.description: A jettison area is one area in which aircrews release hung stores and other stores before they land.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives clearance to release stores in the area.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the aircraft when they release stores, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that aircrews use for the clearance.

heading.description: This field gives the heading of the aircraft when they release stores, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

id.description: This field identifies this area. Each area in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this area.

measure.description: This field identifies the control measure that gives the area.

stores.description: This list contains the stores that aircrews can release in the area.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the area is available.

JettisonArea.title: JettisonArea

LaserCodeAllocation.description: A laser code allocation is one laser code and the units, flights or agencies that use it.

agencies.description: This list identifies the command and control agencies that use the code.

code.description: This field gives the laser code, as a laser code with its unit.

flights.description: This list identifies the flights of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the code. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

units.description: This list identifies the units of the task organization that use the code.

use.description: This field gives the purpose of the code, as one of the enumerated values.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the allocation is in effect.

LaserCodeAllocation.title: LaserCodeAllocation

LasingRestriction.description: A laser restriction is one area and time interval in which a laser has limits.

id.description: This field identifies this restriction. Each restriction in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this restriction.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the restriction, as one of the enumerated values.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area of the restriction.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the lowest altitude for a laser from an aircraft, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the restriction, as free text.

target_lines.description: This list contains the sectors of laser target lines that aircrews can use in the area.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the restriction is in effect.

LasingRestriction.title: LasingRestriction

LightingRule.description: A lighting rule is the condition of the aircraft lights in one phase of flight.

id.description: This field identifies this rule. Each rule in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this rule.

lights.description: This list contains the aircraft lights of the rule.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area of the rule.

phase.description: This field gives the phase of flight of the rule, as one of the enumerated values.

setting.description: This field gives the condition of the aircraft lights, as one of the enumerated values.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the rule is in effect.

LightingRule.title: LightingRule

LightsOutArea.description: A lights-out area is one area in which the aircraft lights are off.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the area, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that fly in the area. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

id.description: This field identifies this area. Each area in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this area.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the area is in effect.

LightsOutArea.title: LightsOutArea

LostCommunicationProcedure.description: A lost communication procedure is the steps that aircrews do when they cannot speak to an agency.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that aircrews cannot speak to.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the procedure. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

id.description: This field identifies this procedure. Each procedure in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this procedure.

phases.description: This list identifies the phases of the operation that the procedure is applicable to.

steps.description: This list contains the steps, in order.

LostCommunicationProcedure.title: LostCommunicationProcedure

LostCommunicationStep.description: A lost communication step is one step of a lost communication procedure.

action.description: This field gives the task of the step, as one of the enumerated values.

after_minutes.description: This field gives the time from the start of the lost communication to the step, in minutes.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that the aircraft lands at.

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the step, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

measure.description: This field identifies the control measure that is the point or the area of the step.

route.description: This field identifies the route of the resource catalogue that the aircraft flies.

squawk.description: This field gives the Mode 3/A code that the aircraft sets, as four octal digits.

LostCommunicationStep.title: LostCommunicationStep

NvgProcedure.description: A night vision goggles (NVG) procedure is the procedure for flight with NVG in one area and time interval.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the procedure. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

id.description: This field identifies this procedure. Each procedure in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this procedure.

lighting.description: This field gives the lighting of the aircraft, as one of the enumerated values.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that give the area of the procedure.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the lowest altitude for flight with night vision goggles (NVG), as an altitude with its unit and reference.

minimum_illumination.description: This field gives the lowest illumination of the moon for flight with night vision goggles (NVG), in percent.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the procedure is in effect.

NvgProcedure.title: NvgProcedure

OrderLinks.description: Order links are the orders that this document uses. Validation finds each mission reference in the air tasking order (ATO) that this field identifies. References to units, phases and protected sites of an operation order (OPORD) use the OPORD that this field identifies.

aco.description: This field identifies the airspace control order (ACO) that this document uses.

ato.description: This field identifies the air tasking order (ATO) that this document uses.

opord.description: This field identifies the operation order (OPORD) that this document uses.

spins.description: This field identifies the special instructions (SPINS) publication that this document uses.

OrderLinks.title: OrderLinks

OrderRef.description: An order reference is the identifier and the revision of one order.

id.description: This field identifies the order that this reference is for. The value is the `meta.id` field of the order.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the order. The value is the `meta.revision` field of the order.

OrderRef.title: OrderRef

PrintExtension.description: A print extension is the page data that `opord-builder` puts on each printed page of the order. The namespace is `org.opord-builder.print`, and the group is for this application only.

classification_banner.description: This field gives the classification marking on the top and the bottom of each page.

classification_caveat.description: This field gives the dissemination caveat after the classification marking, such as `REL TO USA, FVEY`, as free text.

copy_number.description: This field gives the number of this copy in the distribution. The number should not be more than `number_of_copies`.

logo.description: This field gives the path or the web address of the logo for the cover page.

message_reference_number.description: This field gives the message reference number that the originator gives to the order, as free text.

number_of_copies.description: This field gives the number of copies in the distribution.

page_icon.description: This field gives the path or the web address of the icon for the header of each page.

place_of_issue.description: This field gives the place where the order is issued, as free text.

watermark.description: This field gives the watermark of each page: short text such as `DRAFT`, or the path or the web address of an image.

PrintExtension.title: PrintExtension

ProtectedSite.description: A protected site is one site that the operation keeps safe from attack.

id.description: This field identifies this site. Each site in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this site.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the site, as one of the enumerated values.

measure.description: This field identifies the control measure that gives the area of the site.

name.description: This field gives the name of this site, for display.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the site, as latitude and longitude.

restriction.description: This field gives the restriction on attacks against the site, as one of the enumerated values.

ProtectedSite.title: ProtectedSite

PublicationChange.description: A change is one change to the base publication.

op.description: This field gives the operation of the change, as one of the enumerated values.

path.description: This field gives the location of the change, as a JSON Pointer of `RFC 6901`.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the change, as free text.

value.description: This field gives the new value at the location. An `add` or `replace` change shall have this field. A `remove` change shall not have this field.

PublicationChange.title: PublicationChange

RecoveryAirfield.description: A recovery airfield is one airfield for aircraft that come back, with its entry point and its procedure.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that receives the aircraft.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the airfield. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that aircraft use for the recovery.

entry_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the entry point to the airfield. The point shall have the role `control` or `gate` or `marshalling`.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of this entry. The value 1 is the highest priority.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure of the resource catalogue that gives the steps of the recovery.

route.description: This field identifies the route of the resource catalogue that aircraft fly to the airfield.

RecoveryAirfield.title: RecoveryAirfield

RecoveryAuthentication.description: A recovery authentication is the authentication values of isolated personnel for one time interval.

letter.description: This field gives the letter of the day.

number.description: This field gives the number of the day, from 0 to 9.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the values are in effect.

word.description: This field gives the word of the day, as free text.

RecoveryAuthentication.title: RecoveryAuthentication

ReportRequirement.description: A report requirement is one report that units send, with its time and recipient.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that send the report. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that sends the report.

due.description: This field gives the time of the first report.

from_units.description: This list identifies the units of the task organization that send the report.

interval_minutes.description: This field gives the time between two reports, in minutes.

report.description: This field identifies the report of the resource catalogue that this requirement is for.

to_agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the report.

to_unit.description: This field identifies the unit of the task organization that receives the report.

trigger.description: This field gives the event that causes the report, as free text.

ReportRequirement.title: ReportRequirement

RestrictedFrequency.description: A restricted frequency is one entry of the restricted frequency list.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls the frequency.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that the restriction is for.

frequency.description: This field gives the frequency of the restriction, when no channel identifies it, as a frequency with its unit.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the restriction, as one of the enumerated values.

RestrictedFrequency.title: RestrictedFrequency

ReturnToForce.description: A return-to-force procedure is the safe passage of friendly aircraft back through friendly air defence.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls the safe passage.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the route back, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the procedure. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that aircraft use on the route back.

checkpoints.description: This list identifies the points that are the identification checkpoints on the route back. Each point shall have the role `identification_safety`.

id.description: This field identifies this procedure. Each procedure in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this procedure.

maximum_speed.description: This field gives the maximum speed in the safe lanes, as a speed with its unit.

name.description: This field gives the name of this procedure, for display.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the procedure, as free text.

routes.description: This list identifies the control measures that are minimum-risk routes and corridors back to friendly forces. Each measure shall have the type `MRR` or `SC` or `TC` or `AIRCOR` or `SAAFR` or `LLTR`.

safe_lanes.description: This list identifies the control measures that are safe lanes through friendly air defence. Each measure shall have the type `SL`.

squawk.description: This field gives the Mode 3/A code that aircraft set on the route back, as four octal digits.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the procedure is in effect.

ReturnToForce.title: ReturnToForce

RoeRule.description: A rule of engagement is one rule of the rules of engagement (ROE), with its number and its control measures.

id.description: This field identifies this rule. Each rule in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this rule.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that the rule is applicable to.

number.description: This field gives the number of the rule in the rules of engagement (ROE), such as `R-101`, as free text.

rule.description: This field gives the rule, as free text.

units.description: This list identifies the units of the task organization that the rule is applicable to.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the rule is in effect.

RoeRule.title: RoeRule

SpinsAirDefense.description: A special instructions (SPINS) air defence is the air defence procedures for aircrews. It uses the weapons control orders and the air defence warnings of Annex D, Appendix 7, of the operation order (OPORD).

commit_criteria.description: This list contains the commit criteria.

engagement_authorities.description: This list identifies the command and control agencies that have engagement authority.

identification_matrix.description: This list contains the rows of the identification matrix.

return_to_force.description: This list contains the return-to-force procedures.

summary.description: This field gives the summary of the air defence procedures, as free text.

warnings.description: This list contains the air defence warnings.

weapons_control.description: This list contains the weapons control orders.

SpinsAirDefense.title: SpinsAirDefense

SpinsCas.description: Special instructions (SPINS) close air support (CAS) and laser procedures are the CAS stacks, the laser code plan and the laser restrictions.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the entries of the laser code plan.

lasing_restrictions.description: This list contains the laser restrictions.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the close air support (CAS) and laser procedures, as free text.

stacks.description: This list contains the close air support (CAS) stacks.

SpinsCas.title: SpinsCas

SpinsCommunications.description: Special instructions (SPINS) communications are the radio nets and the brevity words.

brevity.description: This list contains the brevity words of the operation.

nets.description: This list contains the radio nets.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about communications, as free text.

SpinsCommunications.title: SpinsCommunications

SpinsDivertAbort.description: Special instructions (SPINS) diversion data is the abort conditions and the divert airfields.

abort_code.description: This field gives the abort code, as free text.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the abort conditions.

divert_airfields.description: This list contains the divert airfields, in order.

SpinsDivertAbort.title: SpinsDivertAbort

SpinsElectromagnetic.description: A special instructions (SPINS) emission control and electromagnetic attack is the emission control periods and the jamming coordination. It uses the types of Annex C, Appendix 12, of the operation order (OPORD).

emission_control.description: This list contains the emission control periods, in order.

jamming.description: This list contains the jamming coordination entries.

jamming_authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives approval for electromagnetic attack.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the emission control and electromagnetic attack procedures, as free text.

SpinsElectromagnetic.title: SpinsElectromagnetic

SpinsEmergency.description: Special instructions (SPINS) emergency procedures are the jettison areas, the routes for aircraft with damage and the lost communication procedures.

damaged_aircraft_routes.description: This list contains the routes for aircraft with damage.

jettison_areas.description: This list contains the jettison areas.

lost_communication.description: This list contains the lost communication procedures.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the emergency procedures, as free text.

SpinsEmergency.title: SpinsEmergency

SpinsIdentification.description: A special instructions (SPINS) identification is the identification, friend or foe (IFF) assignments and code words.

code_words.description: This list contains the code words.

iff.description: This list contains the identification, friend or foe (IFF) assignments.

SpinsIdentification.title: SpinsIdentification

SpinsNet.description: A special instructions (SPINS) net is one radio net for aircrews.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls the net.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that the net refers to.

id.description: This field identifies this net. Each net in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this net.

name.description: This field gives the name of this net, for display.

purpose.description: This field gives the purpose of the net, as free text.

SpinsNet.title: SpinsNet

SpinsNight.description: Special instructions (SPINS) night procedures are the night vision goggles (NVG) procedures, the lights-out areas and the lighting rules.

lighting.description: This list contains the lighting rules.

lights_out_areas.description: This list contains the lights-out areas.

nvg.description: This list contains the night vision goggles (NVG) procedures.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the night procedures, as free text.

SpinsNight.title: SpinsNight

SpinsRecovery.description: A special instructions (SPINS) personnel recovery is the combat search and rescue (CSAR) and personnel recovery procedures.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls personnel recovery.

authentication.description: This list contains the authentication values, in order.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that are for isolated personnel and rescue forces.

isoprep.description: This field gives the identifier of the isolated personnel report (ISOPREP) data for recovery forces. The publication does not contain data that identifies a person.

procedures.description: This list identifies the procedures of the resource catalogue that are for isolated personnel and rescue forces.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about personnel recovery, as free text.

rescue_forces.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that are rescue forces. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

safe_areas.description: This list identifies the control measures that are safe areas for isolated personnel.

SpinsRecovery.title: SpinsRecovery

SpinsRecoveryRouting.description: Special instructions (SPINS) recovery routes are the identification, friend or foe (IFF) lines, the routes back and the recovery airfields.

iff_lines.description: This list identifies the control measures that are lines at which aircraft set the identification, friend or foe (IFF) on or off. Each measure shall have the type `IFFON` or `IFFOFF`.

recovery_airfields.description: This list contains the recovery airfields, in order.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the recovery routes, as free text.

return_routes.description: This list identifies the control measures that are routes back to friendly airspace. Each measure shall have the type `MRR` or `SC` or `TC` or `AIRCOR` or `SAAFR` or `LLTR`.

routes.description: This list identifies the routes of the resource catalogue that aircraft fly back to the airfields.

SpinsRecoveryRouting.title: SpinsRecoveryRouting

SpinsRestrictions.description: Special instructions (SPINS) restrictions are the sites that aircrews do not attack and the weather minimums.

other_protected_sites.description: This list contains the protected sites that the operation order (OPORD) does not give.

protected_sites.description: This list identifies the protected sites of Annex K of the operation order (OPORD) that aircrews do not attack. The `orders` field identifies the OPORD.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the restrictions, as free text.

weather_minimums.description: This list contains the weather minimums.

SpinsRestrictions.title: SpinsRestrictions

SpinsRoe.description: A special instructions (SPINS) rules of engagement (ROE) summary is the ROE summary for aircrews.

measures.description: This list identifies the control measures that the rules of engagement (ROE) refer to.

rules.description: This list contains the rules of engagement (ROE).

summary.description: This field gives the summary of the rules of engagement (ROE), as free text.

SpinsRoe.title: SpinsRoe

StackBlock.description: A stack level is one altitude block of a close air support (CAS) stack and the missions that use it.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the level, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that use the level. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

use.description: This field gives the purpose of the level, as one of the enumerated values.

StackBlock.title: StackBlock

TankerProcedure.description: A tanker procedure is the procedure for one refuelling track or anchor.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the refuelling, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that are tanker missions on the track. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that are for the tanker and receivers.

id.description: This field identifies this procedure. Each procedure in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this procedure.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure of the resource catalogue that gives the rendezvous steps.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the procedure, as free text.

tacan.description: This field gives the channel of the tanker for Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN).

track.description: This field identifies the orbit that is the refuelling track or anchor. The measure shall be an orbit.

TankerProcedure.title: TankerProcedure

WeaponsControl.description: A weapons control order is one weapons control status for an area and a time interval.

measure.description: This field identifies the control measure that gives the area of the weapons control status.

status.description: This field gives the weapons control status, as one of the enumerated values.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the weapons control status is in effect.

WeaponsControl.title: WeaponsControl

WeatherMinimum.description: A weather minimum is the lowest ceiling and visibility for one type of tasking or one phase of flight.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that the minimum is applicable to.

ato_missions.description: This list identifies the missions of the air tasking order (ATO) that the minimum is applicable to. The `orders` field identifies the ATO.

ceiling.description: This field gives the lowest height of the cloud base above the ground, as a length with its unit.

id.description: This field identifies this minimum. Each minimum in the publication has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this minimum.

phase.description: This field gives the phase of flight that the minimum is applicable to, as one of the enumerated values.

taskings.description: This list contains the types of typed tasking that the minimum is applicable to.

visibility.description: This field gives the lowest flight visibility, as a length with its unit.

WeatherMinimum.title: WeatherMinimum

airspace.description: Airspace is a region of airspace with a name, made of volumes that each have a horizontal boundary and vertical limits. The `airspace_type` field gives the class or the type of operation. Shelves, sectors and subtracted volumes use the same structure of components. The control measures for air traffic in Annex B use this contract. Examples are class B airspace, control zones and restricted areas.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

airspace_class_code.description: This field gives the airspace class that the source gives, as one of the enumerated values. When the code is empty, the source gives no class. All classes use the same structure for geometry and altitude.

airspace_type.description: This field gives the class or type of operation of the airspace, such as `ClassB`, `ClassD`, `MTA` or `TMA`, as one of the enumerated values. `MTA` is a military training area, and `TMA` is a terminal control area.

x-enum-descriptions.ADIZ: An air defence identification zone (ADIZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the identification, location and control of aircraft is immediately necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ATCAA: An air traffic control assigned airspace (ATCAA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral limits that air traffic control (ATC) assigns. It separates the stated activities in it from other instrument flight rules (IFR) air traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.ATZ: An aerodrome traffic zone (ATZ) is airspace of defined dimensions around an aerodrome. Its function is the protection of aerodrome traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.Alert: An alert area is airspace that can contain a large quantity of pilot training or an unusual type of flight. This training and these flights are not dangerous to aircraft. Charts show the area to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about it. All flights in it obey the Code of Federal Regulations. Each pilot in it has the same task of collision avoidance.
x-enum-descriptions.CFA: A controlled firing area (CFA) is airspace that contains activities that are a danger to non-participating aircraft when they are not in a controlled environment. They stop at once when spotter aircraft, radar or ground observers find an aircraft that approaches.
x-enum-descriptions.CTA: A control area (CTA) is controlled airspace that extends upwards from a given limit above the surface. Its floor is above the surface, not at the surface. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.CTR: A control zone (CTR) is controlled airspace from the surface to a given upper limit. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassA: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class A airspace is airspace only for instrument flight rules (IFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassB: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class B airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other. In the United States, ATC separates VFR flights with radar. When the radar does not operate, ATC stops this service for VFR flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassC: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class C airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights from all other flights, and VFR flights from IFR flights. VFR flights get traffic information about other VFR flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassD: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class D airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. IFR flights get traffic information about VFR flights, and VFR flights get traffic information about all other flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassE: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class E airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. Only IFR flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary only for IFR flights. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. All flights get traffic information as far as practical. A control zone cannot be class E airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassF: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class F airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. Participating IFR flights get an air traffic advisory service, which separates them from other IFR flights as far as practical. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it. The United States does not use class F airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassG: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class G airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service or separation, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it.
x-enum-descriptions.Danger: A danger area is airspace of defined dimensions in which tasks that are dangerous to the flight of aircraft can occur at stated times. This definition comes from air traffic control.
x-enum-descriptions.FIR: A flight information region (FIR) is airspace of defined dimensions in which flight information service and alerting service are available.
x-enum-descriptions.MOA: A military operations area (MOA) is airspace that is not in class A airspace. It separates flight training of armed forces that is not dangerous from instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft. It also shows visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft where this training occurs. When it is active, air traffic control (ATC) lets an IFR flight go through it only when ATC can separate the flight.
x-enum-descriptions.MTA: A military training area (MTA) is a geographical area that is temporarily or permanently for education and training, which includes exercises and testing. It can include airspace. AJP-3.3.5 gives this area as the training area (TRNG).
x-enum-descriptions.ModeCVeil: A mode C veil is the airspace that is 30 nautical miles or less from an airport in Appendix D, section 1 of 14 CFR part 91. It goes from the surface to 10,000 feet above mean sea level (MSL). Unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes a different procedure, aircraft in it have a serviceable transponder with automatic altitude reporting and serviceable `ADS-B Out` equipment.
x-enum-descriptions.NSA: A national security area (NSA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral dimensions at locations with ground facilities. At these locations, it is necessary to increase security and safety. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) tells pilots to avoid flight through it. A temporary flight restriction (TFR) can temporarily close it to flight.
x-enum-descriptions.Other: The airspace has a local type that is not in this list. The `local_type` field gives the local name of the type.
x-enum-descriptions.Prohibited: A prohibited area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. The state prohibits flight in it.
x-enum-descriptions.RMZ: A radio mandatory zone (RMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of radio equipment is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.ROZ: A restricted operating zone (ROZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates for a given situation or operational need. Examples are refuelling orbits, holding, fires and landing or drop zones. It restricts the operation of one or more airspace users in it.
x-enum-descriptions.Restricted: A restricted area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. In it, the conditions that the state gives restrict the flight of aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.SFRA: A special flight rules area (SFRA) is airspace of defined dimensions, above land areas or territorial waters. In it, the flight of aircraft obeys 14 CFR part 93, unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions.Sector: A control sector is airspace of known horizontal and vertical dimensions. One controller or a group of controllers controls the air traffic in it. The primary traffic flows, the altitude layers and the work of the controllers set its limits. Pilots in it usually speak to air traffic control (ATC) on the frequencies of the sector.
x-enum-descriptions.TFR: A temporary flight restriction (TFR) is a regulatory action of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a notice to air missions (NOTAM). It temporarily restricts some aircraft from operation in a defined area. Its function is the protection of persons or property in the air or on the ground.
x-enum-descriptions.TMA: A terminal control area (TMA) is a control area, usually at the confluence of air traffic services routes near one or more major aerodromes. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.TMZ: A transponder mandatory zone (TMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of a pressure-altitude reporting transponder is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.TRA: A temporary reserved area (TRA) is a defined volume of airspace that one airspace authority usually controls. By common agreement, it is temporarily for another airspace authority. Other air traffic may transit it only with air traffic control (ATC) clearance.
x-enum-descriptions.TRSA: A terminal radar service area (TRSA) is airspace around a designated airport. In it, air traffic control (ATC) gives radar vectoring, sequencing and separation full time. This service is for all instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft and participating visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft. This service is not mandatory for pilots. It is not an airspace class.
x-enum-descriptions.TSA: A temporary segregated area (TSA) is airspace of defined dimensions for the exclusive use of specified users. Their tasks make this necessary. It is for a set period, and no other traffic uses the airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.UIR: An upper flight information region (UIR) is a flight information region (FIR) above a different FIR. Its floor is the ceiling of the lower FIR and is a visual flight rules (VFR) cruising level. Its procedures can be different from the procedures of the lower FIR.
x-enum-descriptions.Warning: A warning area is airspace of known dimensions that starts 3 nautical miles from the coast of the United States. It contains tasks that can be dangerous to non-participating aircraft. Its function is to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about this risk. It can be above the waters of the United States, above international waters or above the two.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace.

components.description: This list contains the airspace volumes of this airspace, in order. Each volume has a floor and a ceiling.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this airspace and its local conditions, as free text.

designator.description: This field gives the designator that a publication or an assignment gives to the airspace. An example is the designator of a restricted area.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airspace. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace.

local_type.description: This field gives the local type name of the airspace when `airspace_type` is `Other`, as free text.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airspace, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace.

state.description: This field gives the State responsible for the airspace, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code such as `DEU`. Under International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 11, paragraph 2.1, this State is responsible for the air traffic services in the airspace. An example is the State of a flight information region (FIR).

type.description: The value identifies this record as an airspace, which is a region made of airspace volumes.

airspace.title: Airspace

airway.description: An airway is an en-route route as a sequence of fixes, with the course, the distance and the altitude limits of each segment.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

airway_type.description: This field gives the class of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.advisory: This value identifies a designated route along which air traffic advisory service is available.
x-enum-descriptions.air_traffic_services: This value identifies a specified route that channels the flow of traffic, as necessary to supply air traffic services.
x-enum-descriptions.airway: This value identifies a control area, or a part of it, in the shape of a corridor. Radio navigation aids identify the corridor.
x-enum-descriptions.area_navigation: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route for aircraft that can do area navigation.
x-enum-descriptions.conditional: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route, or a part of it, that is non-permanent. Aircraft plan and use it only under stated conditions.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this airway.

ident.description: This field identifies this airway as published. An example is `V356`.

level.description: This field gives the altitude structure of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.both: This value identifies the low and the high altitude structures.
x-enum-descriptions.high: This value identifies the high altitude structure.
x-enum-descriptions.low: This value identifies the low altitude structure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airway, for display.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this airway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

segments.description: This list contains the fixes, in airway sequence, in order. Each item has a fix and the segment from that fix to the next fix.

items.description: An airway segment is one airway fix and the segment from this fix to the next fix.

directional_restriction.description: This field gives the direction restriction of the segment, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.backward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in the direction opposite to airway sequence.
x-enum-descriptions.forward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in airway sequence.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from this fix to the next fix, as a length with its unit.

fix.description: This field gives the airway fix at the start of this segment.

inbound_course.description: This field gives the course to this fix from the previous fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

maximum_altitude.description: This field gives the maximum authorized altitude (MAA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the minimum en-route altitude (MEA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

outbound_course.description: This field gives the course from this fix to the next fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure for an airway, with the catalogue code `AIRWAY`. The value selects this contract in a catalogue of control measures.

airway.title: Airway

common.description: Definitions for all openAIX documents are the identifiers, positions, geometry, units, time intervals and resource references that more than one type of document contains.
common.title: openAIX common resources

common.Activation.description: An activation is the time when a control measure is available. It is an interval, a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in an interval, or continuous activation.

continuous.description: The value is `true` when the control measure is active all the time, with no scheduled period in which it is not active.

common.AirspaceComponent.description: An airspace component is one part of an airspace in three dimensions, with a boundary, a floor and a ceiling. Each component adds a volume, subtracts a volume or intersects a volume, in sequence.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this component is available, in the time interval of the parent control measure. This field is optional.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal boundary of this component: points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator. A `geojson` geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.

id.description: This field identifies this component. Each component in its parent airspace has a different identifier.

lower_limit.description: This field gives the floor of this component: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

maximum_limit.description: This field gives the maximum limit of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `upper_limit`, it increases the ceiling. Each value keeps its reference.

minimum_limit.description: This field gives the minimum floor of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `lower_limit`, it replaces the floor. To compare limits with different references, a consumer uses terrain or atmospheric data.

name.description: This field gives the name of this sector or shelf, for display.

operation.description: This field gives the operation of this component on the volume that the components before it make, as one of the enumerated values. The components operate in the sequence of the array, and the first component adds a volume.

upper_limit.description: This field gives the ceiling of this component: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.Altitude.description: An altitude is a vertical position with its unit and its reference: mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

reference.description: This field gives the vertical reference of the altitude, as one of the enumerated values. The value is mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the altitude: feet, metres or flight level, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the altitude, in the unit of `unit`.

common.Altitude.title: Altitude

common.AltitudeBlock.description: An altitude block is a vertical band between a floor and a ceiling. The floor can be the surface, and the ceiling can have no limit.

lower.description: This field gives the floor of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

upper.description: This field gives the ceiling of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.AltitudeBlock.title: AltitudeBlock

common.Bearing.description: A bearing is a direction with its value and its north reference: true north or magnetic north. A magnetic bearing keeps the reference that its author gives. The declination is optional. When the declination is not available, a consumer should show that it cannot change the bearing to true north.

declination_deg.description: This field gives the magnetic declination that changes a bearing from true north to magnetic north, in degrees. This field is optional.

reference.description: This field gives the north reference of the bearing: true north or magnetic north, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the bearing, in degrees from 0 to less than 360.

common.BearingRange.description: A bearing range is a range of bearings from a start bearing clockwise to an end bearing.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the end of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the start of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

common.CasBrief.description: A close air support (CAS) brief is the data that the aircrew get for one CAS attack: the 9-line data of JP 3-09.3 and the mission-level data of the air tasking order (ATO). The ATO and the operation order (OPORD) use this one definition. A field that a use does not need stays out of the record. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Chapter V gives the check-in briefing and the CAS brief.

ato_mission.description: This field identifies the mission of the air tasking order (ATO) that receives the brief. The `orders` field of the operation order (OPORD) identifies the ATO.

check_in.description: This field gives the check-in data for the controller.

contact_points.description: This list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role `control`.

control_type.description: This field gives the type of terminal attack control, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.type_1: This value identifies type 1 terminal attack control, in which the controller sees the target and the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_2: This value identifies type 2 terminal attack control, in which the controller does not see the target or the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_3: This value identifies type 3 terminal attack control, in which the controller gives clearance for all attacks in an area.

controller.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives the brief.

controllers.description: This list contains the agencies and radio channels that control the close air support (CAS) for this brief.

danger_close.description: The value is `true` when the friendly forces are inside the danger-close distance of the weapons for the attack. The value is `false` when the friendly forces are outside that distance.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from the initial point to the target, as a length with its unit.

egress_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the egress point. The point shall have the role `egress`.

final_attack_headings.description: This list contains the ranges of final attack headings that the aircraft can use for the attack. Each range goes clockwise from its start bearing to its end bearing.

fire_support_measures.description: This list identifies the fire support coordination measures that apply to the close air support (CAS) mission.

friendly_direction.description: This field gives the direction from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

friendly_distance.description: This field gives the distance from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as a length with its unit.

friendly_lines.description: This list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.

friendly_marking.description: This field gives the means that marks the position of the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

ground_scheme_summary.description: This field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.

hazards.description: This list contains the hazards in the target area that are not threats.

heading.description: This field gives the heading from the initial point to the target, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.

holding_altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

id.description: This field identifies this close air support (CAS) brief. Each CAS brief in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this CAS brief.

initial_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the initial point of the attack. The point shall have the role `initial`.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the aircraft. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

laser_code.description: This field gives the code of the laser mark, as a laser code with its unit.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this brief.

laser_target_line.description: This field gives the laser target line, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

mark.description: This field gives the type of mark of the target, as one of the enumerated values.

marks.description: This list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.

method_of_attack.description: This field gives the method of attack, as one of the enumerated values.

offset_direction.description: This field gives the side of the line from the initial point to the target on which the aircraft fly the attack, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.left: The aircraft fly the attack to the left of the line from the initial point to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.right: The aircraft fly the attack to the right of the line from the initial point to the target.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

target.description: This field identifies the target of the resource catalogue that the brief is for.

target_description.description: This field gives the target description, as free text.

target_elevation.description: This field gives the elevation of the target, as an elevation with its unit.

target_position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the target, as latitude and longitude.

threats.description: This list identifies the threats of the resource catalogue that are a danger to the aircraft in the target area.

time_on_target.description: This field gives the time at which the weapons hit the target.

time_to_target_seconds.description: This field gives the time from the time of the brief to the time on target, in seconds.

common.CheckIn.description: A close air support (CAS) check-in is the data that the CAS aircrew gives to the controller at check-in. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Figure V-4 gives the check-in briefing.

abort_code.description: This field gives the abort code for the controller and the aircrew, as free text.

items.description: This list contains the parts of the check-in briefing that the aircrew gives.

x-enum-descriptions.abort_code: This value identifies the code that the aircrew uses to make sure that an abort call comes from the controller.
x-enum-descriptions.aircraft_number_and_type: This value identifies the quantity of aircraft in the flight and their aircraft type.
x-enum-descriptions.capabilities: This value identifies the sensors and the other capabilities of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.mission_number: This value identifies the mission number of the flight in the air tasking order (ATO).
x-enum-descriptions.ordnance: This value identifies the weapons on the aircraft, with the quantity of each.
x-enum-descriptions.position_and_altitude: This value identifies the position of the flight at this time, usually from a control point, and its altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.time_on_station: This value identifies the time that the aircraft can stay on station.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the check-in steps.

common.ClassificationLevel.description: A classification level is a security classification of the American government that the banner of an operation order (OPORD) can show.
common.ClassificationLevel.title: ClassificationLevel

common.Coalition.description: A coalition is the side of a record in the simulation: `blue`, `red` or `neutral`. It is simulator data, not real-world data.

common.ControlMeasure.description: A control measure is one openAIX control measure: a reference to one control measure contract, or an extension control measure with a namespace. The `type` field selects the contract.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which the extension control measure is available. The value is a schedule or a flag for continuous activation.

description.description: This field gives the information about this extension control measure and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the extension control measure: a position or a boundary. The geometry uses points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator, or a GeoJSON geometry (RFC 7946).

id.description: This field identifies this extension control measure. Other records and orders use it to refer to this extension control measure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this extension control measure, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this extension control measure, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this extension control measure. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: This field gives the type of the extension control measure, as a name with a namespace.

id.description: This field identifies the control measure of this selection.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure selection. The value is `control_measure`.

common.ControllerContact.description: An agency channel is an agency for the aircrew, with its radio channels.

agency.description: This field identifies the agency or forward air controller that the aircrew speaks to. The value is the identifier of a command and control agency or of a forward air controller (FAC) of the resource catalogue.

alternate_channel.description: This field identifies the alternative radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency when the primary channel is not available.

channel.description: This field identifies the primary radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency.

common.DCSData.description: Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data is the data of a record for DCS. The `bindings` field contains the objects in a DCS mission that are this record or that show it. The other fields contain DCS values that are not objects of a mission.

alic_code.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft launcher interface computer (ALIC) code of the radar. The high-speed anti-radiation missile (HARM) of the DCS F-16C uses this code. Appendix B of the `DCS F-16C Early Access Guide` gives the codes.

angle_deg.description: This field gives the drawing angle from the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission, in degrees. This angle is not a true bearing or a magnetic bearing. Only a consumer with a correct adapter for DCS should use this angle to turn the shape.

beacon.description: This field gives the radio beacon of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object that the record is bound to: the identification, the frequency and the channel as the DCS database gives them. They can differ from the published values of the real station, which the core fields of the record give. The record has at least one of them.

channel.description: This field gives the channel number of the beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, for a beacon that DCS tunes by channel, for example a `TACAN`, an `RSBN` or a landing radio beacon group (PRMG) beacon.

frequency.description: This field gives the frequency of the beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, as a frequency with its unit.

ident.description: This field identifies this beacon in the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) database, as the DCS radio transmits it in Morse code.

bindings.description: This list contains the objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are this record or show it on the map. The record keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of these objects.

clsid.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifier (CLSID) of the load on the pylon. For a rack, the CLSID identifies the rack together with its stores.
